questions.prompt: Why should date/time code make its time-zone assumptions explicit?
options: Intl methods remove all differences between time zones.
Local time, UTC, daylight-saving rules and display locale can change the interpreted or displayed value.
Date objects store the user’s preferred language automatically.
Every ISO-looking date string always uses local time.
questions.explanation: Use defined timestamps and explicit formatting/time-zone decisions for consistent results.

questions.prompt: When rendering untrusted user-provided plain text, what should be avoided?
options: Validating data at the server boundary.
Interpreting it as HTML with innerHTML without a suitable sanitization/trust policy.
questions.explanation: HTML injection can turn untrusted strings into markup; safe rendering and contextual validation reduce risk.
